trials.title: FIGHT-202 (pemigatinib in previously treated CCA)
trials.notes: Pivotal registration trial, now closed. Listed for context, not as an enrollment path.

manufacturer.notes: IncyteCARES Oncology patient-assistance line is 1-855-452-5234 (Mon-Fri 8am-8pm ET) for benefits review and copay help.

payer_access_notes: On-label use for an FGFR2-positive result is routinely covered; an FDA-approved companion test result is part of the label. IncyteCARES handles benefits review and copay assistance. If the FGFR2 test is negative, this drug is not indicated.
access_summary: If comprehensive profiling returns an FGFR2 fusion or rearrangement, pemigatinib becomes standard second-line therapy a treating oncologist can prescribe directly, no trial needed. The whole path hinges on that one positive test, which is exactly the rank-1 workup this case is waiting on.
next_steps: Order RNA-based fusion NGS (or DNA NGS with fusion calling) and confirm an FGFR2 fusion or rearrangement on an FDA-approved test.
If positive, the treating oncologist writes a standard prescription and enrolls the patient in IncyteCARES at 1-855-452-5234 for benefits and copay support.
Plan baseline and serial ophthalmologic exams and phosphate monitoring before starting.
Call Incyte Medical Information at 1-855-463-3463 for any dosing or drug-interaction questions.

payer_access_notes: On-label coverage for an FGFR2-positive intrahepatic result is routine; Taiho Oncology Patient Support handles benefits and copay. The label is specific to intrahepatic CCA, so subsite documentation matters for reimbursement.
access_summary: Futibatinib is the other approved FGFR inhibitor, and it holds activity against some kinase-domain mutations that drive resistance to pemigatinib, which makes it useful for sequencing rather than just as an alternative first FGFR drug. Same gate as pemigatinib: a confirmed FGFR2 fusion or rearrangement, and the on-label indication is specific to intrahepatic disease.
next_steps: Confirm an FGFR2 fusion or rearrangement and document intrahepatic subsite, since the label is intrahepatic-specific.
If positive, prescribe directly and enroll in Taiho Oncology Patient Support at 1-844-824-4648.
Consider futibatinib specifically in the post-pemigatinib setting given its activity against some acquired resistance mutations.
Monitor phosphate and schedule ophthalmologic exams per the FGFR class profile.

trials.indication: Advanced CCA with activating FGFR2 alterations, including acquired resistance mutations
trials.notes: Recruiting at UCSF, Massachusetts General Hospital, Ohio State, and MD Anderson. Open to activating FGFR2 alterations including kinase-domain resistance mutations that emerge on first-generation FGFR inhibitors.

manufacturer.notes: Same contact serves trial inquiries; no separate medical-information line exists for an investigational agent.

payer_access_notes: Investigational; trial sponsor covers study-drug costs. No commercial coverage and no off-label path because the drug is not approved.
access_summary: TYRA-200 is a next-generation FGFR2 inhibitor in phase 1, and the only way to get it is enrolling in NCT06160752. It is most relevant if the patient tests FGFR2-positive and later progresses on pemigatinib or futibatinib, since it targets some of the resistance mutations that defeat the approved drugs. No efficacy data have read out yet.
next_steps: Confirm an activating FGFR2 alteration first, since eligibility turns on it.
Email the central contact at TyraClinicalTrials@tyra.bio or call (619) 728-4805 to check slot availability at the nearest of UCSF, MGH, Ohio State, or MD Anderson.
Reserve this option mainly for the post-FGFR-inhibitor resistance setting rather than treatment-naive FGFR2-positive disease, where approved drugs come first.

If positive, prescribe directly and enroll in ServierONE at 1-800-813-5905 for benefits and copay support.

trials.title: DESTINY-PanTumor02 (T-DXd in HER2-expressing solid tumors, incl. biliary cohort)
trials.notes: Registration basket; no longer enrolling. Context only.

manufacturer.notes: 1-877-240-9479 is the AstraZeneca information center (verified via the NCT06467357 registry record). The tumor-agnostic label means biliary use is on-label for HER2 IHC 3+, off-label below that.

payer_access_notes: The tumor-agnostic HER2 IHC 3+ label makes biliary use on-label at IHC 3+. Use at IHC 2+ falls outside the label and is more likely to draw a prior-authorization fight; the DESTINY-PanTumor02 data showed the IHC 3+ subgroup responded far better (about 61% vs 22% overall). Interstitial lung disease is the defining safety risk and was fatal in three patients on the basket study.
access_summary: Because the HER2 IHC 3+ label is tumor-agnostic, T-DXd is effectively on-label for an IHC 3+ biliary tumor once profiling confirms it; below IHC 3+ it shifts to a genuine off-label call. A first-line randomized trial, DESTINY-BTC01 (NCT06467357), is recruiting across US sites for treatment-naive HER2-expressing patients. ILD risk should weigh in the decision even though no toxicity veto was set.
next_steps: Run HER2 IHC with reflex ISH and document the exact IHC score, since 3+ is the on-label threshold and drives expected benefit.
If treatment-naive, call the AstraZeneca center at 1-877-240-9479 to check DESTINY-BTC01 (NCT06467357) slots before defaulting to off-label use.
For IHC 3+ use, the oncologist can prescribe on-label; for IHC 2+ expect a prior-authorization step.
Baseline pulmonary assessment and active ILD/pneumonitis surveillance throughout treatment.

trials.notes: Supporting basket; no longer enrolling. Context only. Pembrolizumab is widely available on-label, so trial enrollment is not the access path for the agnostic biomarkers.

payer_access_notes: On-label coverage requires an FDA-approved MSI-H/dMMR or TMB-high test result. MSI-H/dMMR is the cleaner full-approval path; the TMB-high indication is accelerated and occasionally draws more payer scrutiny. The Merck Access Program assists with prior authorization and copay.
access_summary: If MMR IHC, an MSI assay, or NGS-derived TMB comes back MSI-H/dMMR or TMB-high, pembrolizumab is on-label tumor-agnostic therapy the oncologist can prescribe directly. Both markers are uncommon in biliary cancer (MSI-H roughly 1-3%) but decision-changing when present, and the same comprehensive panel that resolves the other axes returns the TMB value.
next_steps: Run MMR IHC plus reflex MSI assay and confirm TMB on the NGS panel.
If MSI-H/dMMR or TMB-high, prescribe on-label; the MSI-H/dMMR path is the more robust full approval.

trials.notes: The registry record for this NCT is a colorectal-cancer-specific combination trial at MD Anderson (lead: David S. Hong, MD), not the pan-tumor biliary basket the dossier described, and it is no longer recruiting. It does not admit biliary patients. Treat the dossier's basket framing as an upstream contract issue.

manufacturer.notes: 1-800-721-5072 is the BMS Medical Information line. BMS Access Support assists with benefits and prior authorization. No public medical-info email found.

payer_access_notes: No biliary indication exists, so any biliary use is off-label and likely to face prior-authorization hurdles. The published KRYSTAL-1 biliary cohort was small (n=12, ORR about 42%) but supportive. A KRAS G12C inhibitor only applies to G12C; G12D/G12V and other KRAS variants do not qualify.
access_summary: Adagrasib is approved for KRAS G12C NSCLC and colorectal cancer but not for biliary cancer, so a biliary patient with a confirmed G12C would access it off-label, supported by the small published KRYSTAL-1 biliary cohort. KRAS G12C is rare in biliary cancer (roughly 1%), and the registry trial under NCT05722327 is a colorectal-only combination that does not admit biliary patients. A clinical trial remains a reasonable route if an open KRAS G12C basket accepting biliary tumors can be located.
next_steps: Confirm KRAS G12C specifically on tumor DNA NGS; other KRAS variants do not qualify for a G12C inhibitor.
